author: product-requirements-expert
context: Scoping the visit-cancellation feature request into a prd-entry. The request asks for a cancel action beside each upcoming visit on the owner detail page, removing the visit from the pet's record. That is the exact scope of two Non-Goals confirmed deliberate two days ago: NG-4 (deleting an owner, a pet, or a visit) and NG-5 (changing or cancelling a visit once booked). ADR 2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment records the decision and rules on this case directly: 'A future request touching either row proceeds only on an explicit owner decision recorded at intake. The request itself never reopens the row.' The dispatch carries no such decision. Authoring the requirement now would breach the boundary the ADR exists to hold, so I stopped before writing to docs/prd.md.
question: Do you reverse NG-4 and NG-5 to permit visit cancellation? If yes, I will narrow both rows, author REQ-VIS-003, and write the superseding non-goal ADR. If no, the request is declined against the existing boundary. Three sub-points I can resolve either way once you decide, stated so one answer settles the slice: (1) Upcoming cutoff — REQ-VIS-001 already refuses a booking dated today or earlier, so I would define cancellable as visit date later than today, making a same-day visit not cancellable and matching the booking boundary. (2) Confirmation step — I would require an explicit confirmation before removal, since removal is irreversible and no undo exists. (3) Authorization — NG-1 states the sample has no access control and the codebase has none, so cancellation would be open to any reader, same as every other write flow; confirm that consequence is acceptable for an irreversible action.
stop_state: No edit made to docs/prd.md, docs/ubiquitous-language.md, or docs/adr/. Awaiting the owner decision on NG-4 and NG-5 before authoring REQ-VIS-003. Note: my dispatch-start at line 1 carries req_id REQ-VIS-002, which is an existing requirement (earlier visits shown when booking); the correct minted ID for this capability is REQ-VIS-003, used from this record onward.
